title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors and financial entities to apply DORA in practice: building ICT risk management frameworks, classifying and reporting incidents, testing resilience, managing ICT third-party risk and understanding the oversight of critical ICT third-party providers.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and practitioners a practical command of DORA and its technical standards, from management body accountability and the ICT risk management framework to incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party risk. Participants leave able to judge whether arrangements work in practice rather than on paper, and to see the firm's digital resilience the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: DORA's scope, proportionality and place in the EU rulebook, management body accountability, the ICT risk management framework, incident classification and reporting, digital operational resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and the register of information, the oversight framework for critical ICT third-party providers, information sharing, and supervision and enforcement.
Intended Audience: Supervisors, inspectors and ICT risk specialists at national competent authorities
Information security, ICT risk, operational resilience, outsourcing and compliance staff at financial entities
Senior managers and management body members accountable for digital operational resilience
Learning Objectives: Explain DORA's scope, proportionality and relationship with sectoral rules and the NIS2 Directive
Assess an ICT risk management framework and its governance against DORA and its technical standards
Apply the incident classification criteria and reporting timelines to major ICT-related incidents
Evaluate digital operational resilience testing programmes, including threat-led penetration testing
Assess ICT third-party risk management, contractual provisions and the register of information
Explain the oversight of critical ICT third-party providers and the supervisory and enforcement toolkit
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, simulations and supervisory question sets, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors or financial entities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of operational risk, ICT risk or its supervision is helpful. No technical cybersecurity background is required.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (NIS2 Directive)
Basel Committee, Principles for Operational Resilience (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)

modules.title: DORA Foundations: Scope, Proportionality and Architecture
modules.summary: Why DORA harmonises ICT risk rules across the financial sector, which entities it covers, how proportionality and the simplified framework work, and how the Level 1 text is built out through the ESAs' technical standards.
objectives: Identify the financial entities and ICT third-party service providers within DORA's scope
Apply proportionality, including the simplified ICT risk management framework
Navigate DORA's technical standards, guidelines and interaction with sectoral rules
syllabus: From fragmented sectoral rules to a single digital resilience regulation
Financial entities in scope, microenterprises and the simplified framework
Joint ESA technical standards, delegated acts and supervisory convergence
DORA as sector-specific law alongside NIS2 and outsourcing guidelines

modules.title: Management Body Accountability and ICT Governance
modules.summary: The management body's ultimate responsibility for ICT risk under DORA, the role of the ICT risk control function, and how supervisors test whether governance is real rather than nominal.
objectives: Explain the management body's responsibilities for ICT risk, budgets and policies
Assess the independence and resourcing of the ICT risk control function
Challenge board reporting, training and the digital operational resilience strategy
syllabus: Management body duties: approval, oversight, budget and up-to-date ICT knowledge
Digital operational resilience strategy and ICT risk tolerance
Three lines of defence, the ICT risk control function and internal audit
Red flags: delegated accountability, stale strategy and weak board reporting

modules.title: The ICT Risk Management Framework
modules.summary: DORA's core requirements for identifying, protecting against, detecting, responding to and recovering from ICT risk, including asset inventories, backup and restoration, and learning from incidents and tests.
objectives: Map the ICT risk management lifecycle to DORA's requirements
Assess identification, protection, detection, response and recovery capabilities
Evaluate ICT business continuity and backup arrangements against recovery objectives
syllabus: Identification: information and ICT assets, dependencies and critical or important functions
Protection and prevention: access, encryption, patching and change management
Detection, response and recovery, ICT business continuity and backup policies
Learning, evolving and crisis communication after incidents and tests

modules.title: ICT Incident Classification and Reporting
modules.summary: How financial entities manage ICT-related incidents, apply DORA's classification criteria and thresholds, and report major incidents and significant cyber threats, and how supervisors use reports as early warning.
objectives: Apply the classification criteria to determine whether an incident is major
Meet the timelines and content requirements for initial, intermediate and final reports
Use incident reports and root-cause analysis as supervisory intelligence
syllabus: Incident management process, logging, escalation and client communication
Classification criteria: clients, duration, geography, data, criticality and economic impact
Initial notification, intermediate and final reports and voluntary threat notification
Simulation: classifying and reporting a ransomware incident

modules.title: Digital Operational Resilience Testing and TLPT
modules.summary: The risk-based testing programme every in-scope entity must run, and the threat-led penetration testing required of selected entities, including scoping, testers, cross-border recognition and supervisory follow-up.
objectives: Design a proportionate digital operational resilience testing programme
Explain which entities must perform TLPT and how it is scoped and run
Assess test findings, remediation and the attestation process
syllabus: Testing toolkit: vulnerability assessments, scenario tests and source code reviews
TLPT identification, scope, threat intelligence and red team phases
Internal and external testers, pooled testing and mutual recognition
Red flags: narrowed scope, repeat findings and slipping remediation

modules.title: ICT Third-Party Risk and the Register of Information
modules.summary: Managing ICT third-party risk across the contract lifecycle, the mandatory contractual provisions, concentration and exit, and the register of information as both a compliance tool and a supervisory dataset.
objectives: Apply DORA's principles for ICT third-party risk and the third-party risk strategy
Assess contracts against the key provisions, especially for critical or important functions
Maintain and use the register of information, including subcontracting chains
syllabus: Pre-contract due diligence, concentration risk and intragroup providers
Key contractual provisions, audit rights, termination and exit strategies
Register of information: structure, data quality and submission to authorities
Subcontracting of ICT services supporting critical or important functions

modules.title: Oversight of Critical ICT Third-Party Providers
modules.summary: The EU oversight framework for critical ICT third-party providers: designation, the Lead Overseer, joint examination teams, oversight tools and recommendations, and what it means for financial entities and national authorities.
objectives: Explain the criteria and process for designating critical ICT third-party providers
Describe the Lead Overseer's powers, oversight plans and recommendations
Assess the implications for financial entities' own third-party risk management
syllabus: Criticality assessment, designation and the role of the ESAs
Lead Overseer, Joint Oversight Network, Oversight Forum and joint examination teams
Inspections, recommendations, periodic penalty payments and follow-up by authorities
Third-country providers, the subsidiary requirement and residual entity responsibility

modules.title: Supervision, Information Sharing and Enforcement
modules.summary: How competent authorities integrate DORA into risk-based supervision, cyber threat information-sharing arrangements, cooperation with cybersecurity authorities, and the remedial measures and penalties available, ending with a roadmap workshop.
objectives: Integrate DORA into supervisory planning, inspections and firm risk assessment
Explain information-sharing arrangements and cooperation with NIS2 authorities and CSIRTs
Apply remedial measures and administrative penalties proportionately
syllabus: Supervisory planning, ESA peer reviews and convergence on DORA
Cyber threat information-sharing arrangements among financial entities
Cooperation with NIS2 authorities, CSIRTs and other competent authorities
Workshop: a twelve-month DORA supervisory or remediation roadmap

related.title: The EU AI Act and Financial Services (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AI Act for supervisors and financial firms: risk classification, high-risk credit and insurance uses, provider and deployer duties, supervision and compliance programmes.

related.title: EU Payments Regulation: PSD2, PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on EU payments regulation for supervisors and firms, covering PSD2 and EMD2 today and the PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation reform package.

related.title: Big Tech, Embedded Finance and Open Finance
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors to assess big tech, embedded finance and open finance models, and their concentration, conduct and operational risks.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Operational Resilience, Cyber and Critical Third Parties
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' operational resilience, cyber risk, incident response and third-party dependencies, and to shape the authority's resilience strategy.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' exposure to quantum threats, cryptographic inventories and post-quantum migration plans, and to set proportionate expectations.
